cards.text: Josiah, king of Judah, has set the temple in order. Friend, I've got ONE little bakery and I STILL can't find my spatula. After all this, Neco, king of Egypt, marches up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates.

cards.question: Neco king of Egypt is on the march to Carchemish. What does King Josiah do?

answers.text: He goes out to confront Neco
He sends Neco a gift of gold
He stays in Jerusalem to pray

cards.text: Neco sends messengers to Josiah, and the first thing they say is, “What is the issue between you and me, O king of Judah?” That's the king of EGYPT sounding like a guy you just cut off in traffic.

cards.question: Neco's message tells Josiah that Neco has not come against him today.
Neco tells Josiah he's on his way to fight another dynasty. What does Neco say God has told him to do?

cards.text: Then Neco ends with a warning: “So stop opposing God, who is with me, or He will destroy you!” Friend, that is NOT a message you leave on read.

cards.question: After Neco's warning, Josiah turns away from Neco.

cards.text: Instead, Josiah disguises himself to engage Neco in battle. I respect it, because NO disguise on earth could hide this mustache.

cards.question: Josiah won't listen to Neco's warning. But whose mouth did those words really come from?

cards.text: Josiah goes to fight Neco on the Plain of Megiddo. There the archers shoot King Josiah.

cards.question: After the archers shoot him, Josiah tells his servants to keep fighting without him.

cards.text: Josiah says, “Take me away, for I am badly wounded!” His servants take him out of his chariot and put him in his second chariot.

cards.question: Josiah's servants bring him to ___, and that's where he dies.

cards.text: Josiah is buried in the tomb of his fathers. The king who set the temple in order is gone.

cards.question: After King Josiah dies, only his servants mourn for him.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah, a prophet (Jeremiah 1:5), laments over Josiah.

cards.question: Jeremiah laments over King Josiah. What do the male and female singers do?

answers.text: Recite laments over him to this day
Sing praise for his great victories
Stop singing for a full year

cards.question: The singers' laments over Josiah become a statute for Israel. They get written down in the Book of ___.

cards.text: The rest of Josiah's acts, from beginning to end, and his deeds of loving devotion according to the Law of the LORD? Friend, that's a WHOLE other book.

cards.question: The rest of King Josiah's acts are written in another book. Which one?

answers.text: The Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah
The Book of the Wars of the LORD

findings.problem: The card reuses verse 20 when it calls Josiah the king who set the temple in order, but it cites only verse 24. The citation does not cover everything the card tells; the callback could instead be removed so the card relies only on verse 24.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Marking the statement false establishes only that mourning was not limited to Josiah's servants. No card supplies the actual detail from verse 24 that all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for him, leaving an important beat of the passage untold.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
